paragraphs.text: [PDF page 1] Maya for Council Section 1: CAMPAIGN INFORMATION Candidate Full Name: Maya Kornberg Pronouns: She/Her Do you identify as a member of the LGBTQI Community? No NYC City Council District: 39 Full Name of Campaign Committee: Maya for Council Campaign Website: mayaforcouncil.com Campaign Social Media: @mayaforcouncil (Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Bluesky) If endorsed will you display the endorsement of the Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC in your literature whenever you list other endorsements, including on your campaign website? If no, please explain. Yes!

[PDF page 2] Maya for Council Section 2: CANDIDATE EXPERIENCE & INFORMATION What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you are seeking? I’ve spent my whole career working on making democracy work better for the people it is meant to serve. I’ve previously worked for the United Nations Development Program (UNDP) in economic and political development and at the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) helping legislatures around the world develop processes to more effectively engage with the people they represent. As a Senior Fellow and Manager at the Brennan Center for Justice, I work on combating political violence, creating policy solutions that get big money out of our politics, and making Congress and local governments work effectively and responsively. I wrote a book “Inside Congressional Committees” about how we can make the legislative process work better and I’m proud of my research and advocacy leading to changes in campaign finance and legislative procedure nationally. Accordingly, I've publicly called for outside Super PACs and dark money groups to stay out of the race here in District 39. I know how government works and how to fight for it to work more effectively. And my experience teaching graduate and undergraduate students about politics prepares me to explain how government works and inspire people to get involved. I believe that community starts with family, those we are born into and those we create. In October 2024, I became a mom. My spouse and I love being parents and connecting with other parents and families in the district. I am a sister, daughter, spouse, friend, and ally and I am proud to add the role of “mom. ” As a mom raising a child in District 39, I want to fight to make sure my son has the best possible start. In Brooklyn, I’ve dedicated myself to local activism. I’ve been an executive board member of CBID and IND, and I spend weekends campaigning for Democratic candidates at our farmers markets and subway stations and knocking on doors. I love being an active member of local political clubs, the food coop, and other groups that bring together the community in this wonderful district. Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBTQ+ movement, including any concrete achievements for the LGBTQ+ community that you are responsible for in your current, or previous, elected office/s or positions. Some of my work at the Brennan Center for Justice has focused on political violence targeting candidates and electeds, and the disparate impact of violence on candidates and electeds from marginalized groups (including people of color, women, young people, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and religious and ethnic minorities). I led research that raised awareness of this issue and my team has successfully advocated for policy changes and changes to campaign finance laws to support these groups. Up until going on maternity leave in October 2024, I co-chaired the women and gender equity Employee Resource Group (ERG) at the Brennan Center, where we build community and advocate for staff who identify as women or non-binary. Please detail any specific policy proposals you may have that will affect the LGBTQ+ community. If elected to the City Council, I will support the expansion of the Summer Youth Employment Program Pride Initiative to give even more young LGBTQ+ New Yorkers access to summer jobs, internships, and career events in inclusive workplaces. I will unequivocally support legislation that protects and uplifts LGBTQ+ New Yorkers and stand firmly against any attempts to erode the hard-fought progress that has been made. Please list here the union, organizations (community, civic, media, issue groups), LGBTQ+ leaders, and elected officials that have endorsed you. Independent Neighborhood Democrats (IND), Central Brooklyn Independent Democrats (CBID), NYC Organization of Public Sector Retirees, The New Majority NYC, Former Brooklyn Borough President Marty Markowitz, Former Assemblymember Joan Millman (AD-52), Former Assemblymember Jim Brennan (AD-44), Democratic District Leader Doug Schneider (AD-44), Former Council Member David Yassky Have you ever endorsed any LGBTQ+ candidates? Which ones? As a first-time candidate, I haven’t served in any position from which I could endorse candidates, but I was very proud to have organized and canvassed for the passage of Proposition 1 to protect gender equity last fall, while I was pregnant.

[PDF page 3] Maya for Council Section 3: VISION FOR LEADERSHIP Across the nation, and here in NY, we have seen a massive wave of anti LGBTQ+ legislation, particularly targeting the transgender community. If elected, how will you use your platform to protect LGBTQ+ people? What is the role of the office you are seeking in combating these attacks on our community? The Trump Administration and its MAGA allies have launched a disgusting assault on the LGBTQIA+ community with a particular fixation on the transgender community. It is crucial that we not only stand strongly against any attempt to bring the MAGA-driven discrimination and violence against our LGBTQIA+ neighbors to NYC and District 39, but that we actively show support and allyship with the LGBTQIA+ community. This includes increased tracking and prosecution of hate crimes against members of the LGBTQIA+ community, as well as strongly calling out any acts of hate and discrimination. Furthermore, we need to shore up funding for AIDS and HIV prevention and treatment at the city level in the event the Trump Administration sets their sights on cutting federal funds for these lifesaving programs. We have seen significant hate crimes and targeted attacks against LGBTQ+ New Yorkers in recent years. What is the role of the office you are seeking in responding to these acts and how can we work to reduce discrimination in our City? If elected to the City Council, I will use my office to proactively bring attention to the alarming increase in hate crimes against LGBTQ+ New Yorkers, especially amidst the Trump Administration’s ongoing campaign of hate and discrimination against the trans community in particular. I will be a strong advocate for programs that promote community building and allyship with the LGTBQ+ community. I will also push the NYPD to strengthen their investigative and enforcement efforts for hate crimes against the LGBTQ+ community. The NYPD has historically targeted LGBTQ+ community members for arrest or harassment, violating constitutionally protected rights and abusing their discretionary powers in discriminatory ways. Although great efforts have been made by LGBTQ+ community leaders to improve the NYPD Patrol Guide to inform interactions with LGBTQ+ New Yorkers, we continue to see that those guidelines are not being followed. How will you ensure that local law enforcement officials engage appropriately with LGBTQ+ New Yorkers, specifically trans women, and that there is appropriate oversight of the NYPD? We need to increase the sensitivity training given to officers regarding their interactions with the LGBTQ+ community. Officers should be regularly trained on the Patrol Guide updates in conjunction with LGBTQ+ leaders to ensure they understand and follow them. Furthermore, we need to reform our system of oversight for the NYPD so that officers are properly held accountable for their actions, such as continually disregarding updates to the NYPD Patrol Guide specific to interacting with the LGBTQ+ community. The Police Commissioner should not have the power to both overrule the determinations of the Civilian Complaint Review Board and overturn guilty verdicts by Administrative Judges. I know from my work that effective oversight is done in the open, in full view of the public, and that impartiality is paramount to garnering and maintaining public trust. I believe that internal disciplinary authority within the NYPD should be with the Department of Investigation’s Inspector General and that the final authority on disciplinary actions in the NYPD should be independent Administrative Judges. Sex workers are part of our community. Do you agree to uphold the rights of sex workers and support the Sex Worker Protection Act? Would you support the removal of the VICE Squad, which has been found to be violent towards people in the sex trade? I stand with sex workers in their fight for their basic rights and I would proudly support the Sex Worker Protection Act. And accordingly, I do think we need to disband the VICE Squad. Investigators within the current squad that focus on serious crimes such as human trafficking and online crimes against children should be reorganized into other units. Many in our community are refugees and undocumented immigrants. Do you support NYC remaining a sanctuary city and barring city agencies like NYPD from cooperating with ICE? Yes

[PDF page 4] Maya for Council Section 4: RELEVANT POLICY POSITIONS Trans Equity Do you support trans kids playing on sports teams in accordance with their gender identity, in accordance with DOE policy, New York City and State Human Rights Laws, and the NYS Constitution? Why, or why not? Yes Do you support ensuring all individuals, including trans New Yorkers of all ages are able to access medically appropriate health care services, including reproductive health care and gender affirming care regardless of their gender identity? Why, or why not? Yes Funding Do you support continuing and sustaining funding of the Trans Equity Initiative, which provides funding to several community-based organizations for programming provided specifically to transgender, gender non-conforming and non-binary New Yorkers? If no, please explain. Yes Nonprofit organizations play a vital role for LGBTQ+ New Yorkers, serving as trusted community partners for addressing homelessness, hunger, healthcare, education, and more. However, chronic delays in city payments have left many organizations on the brink of collapse, threatening the services LGBTQ+ residents rely on every day. Do you commit to reforms that streamline the bureaucratic process, prioritize timely payments, and support financial stability for nonprofits serving the LGBTQ+ population? If no, please explain. Yes Health Care Will you support increased funding for the NYC Council Ending the Epidemic Initiative and the HIV/AIDS Services Administration? If no, please explain Yes Will you support fully funding NYC Department of Health’s plan to expand PEP & PreP Access? If no, please explain. Yes Housing The LGBTQ+ community is in great need of senior housing for many of our aging population. Would you help with the funding and siting of senior housing for the LGBTQ+ community in your district and across the city? If no, please explain. Yes Will you support increasing funding for both emergency shelter beds and transitional beds for homeless youth, a large percentage of whom are from the LGBTQ+ community? If no, please explain. Yes Law Enforcement Enforcement agencies, such as the NYPD, DOHMH, and DEP, often target LGBTQ+ businesses for aggressive and discriminatory enforcement actions, particularly as part of Multi-Agency Responses to Community Hotspots (MARCH) raids. Do you support changing the way enforcement actions take place to ensure the LGBTQ+ businesses are treated equally by agencies? If no, please explain. Yes The plan to close Rikers and replace it with borough jails is still on the books, but little progress has been made. At the same time, conditions at Rikers have continued to deteriorate, including the collapse of trans affirming units and policies critical to the safety, dignity, and fair treatment of LGBTQ+ people at Rikers. What should be done now to address the issues on Rikers? What is the role of the office you are seeking in moving forward? I believe our incarceration system in this country is shameful and in many cases inhumane, and unfortunately, Rikers Island is the epitome of this in far too many ways. I support the plan to close Rikers Island and instead build more humane borough-based alternatives. I’m very disappointed by recent reports that the City will miss the 2027 deadline. Especially in light of the current delays, we must not allow conditions at Rikers Island to continue to deteriorate for the good of those who will remain in custody there until its closing. We need to

[PDF page 5] ensure that policies that ensure the equal treatment and safety of LGBTQ+ people at Rikers are upheld, even as we fight to close the facility altogether. I will be a dogged representative who can take on any mayoral administration to hold their feet to the fire to meet an updated deadline, while also working with them to get concrete information on delays and how to get the closing back on track.
